To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a one-dimensional heat transfer model may be used to determine the temperature field around a horizontal ground heat exchange system, provided that the heat transfer coefficient in the ground is constant and that the heat source is linear.

the one-dimensional equation of the heat transfer in the ground may be used for modelling the temperature changes of the ground in the vicinity of horizontal pipes of the heat exchange, and that the linear heat source is a good approximation of the heat transfer around a heat exchanger with parallel pipes.
it is possible to model the temperature field in the ground around a horizontal ground heat exchange system with the use of a linear heat source.

the theoretical and experimental analysis of heat transfer processes in a ground heat source with horizontal pipes.
the possibility of using a simplified model for heat transfer in a heat exchanger with pipes embedded in the ground, which may be used in the design of ground heat exchangers.
the possibility of using a simplified model for predicting the temperature of the earth in which a horizontal heat exchanger is placed.

the linear model of heat sources can be used to determine the temperature of the soil around a horizontal pipe of the ground heat exchanger.
the linear heat source theory is a very good model for describing the temperature field around a ground heat exchangers with parallel pipes.
a simplified mathematical model of heat transfer in a horizontal ground heat exchange can be used in practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of a one-dimensional model of heat transfer for the analysis of temperature profiles in the vicinity of horizontal ground heat exchangers is justified, especially when the distance from the level in question to the ground surface is large and the distance between the pipes axes is relatively small.
the linear model of heat source can be applied to describe heat transfer in horizontal pipes of ground heat exchangers, provided that the pipes are arranged in parallel and the heat flux is constant.

the use of the one-dimensional heat transfer model for the analysis of heat exchange in a horizontal heat exchanger in parallel pipes is justified, as long as the distance between the pipes is small and the duration of the process is large.

the use of the one-dimensional equation of the heat conduction in modelling the ground heat exchangers with parallel horizontal pipes is justified.
the temperature profiles for the pipe exchanger are very similar to the profiles for the plate heat exchanger.
